TEXT.TEXTVALUE: We'll require quick lime, distilled water, beakers, spatula, glass rod, test tube, dropper, and lime water.
Take a small quantity of quick lime (Calcium oxide) using a spatula and transfer it into a beaker.
Slowly add water into the beaker so that quick lime remains submerged in the water.
Quick lime reacts vigorously with water to produce a suspension of slaked lime releasing a large amount of heat.
Leave the beaker undisturbed for some time. A clear solution of lime water appears as the suspension of slaked lime settles down to the bottom of the beaker.
A clear solution of lime water appears as the suspension of slaked lime settles down.
Take a small quantity of lime water using a dropper and transfer it into a test tube.
Cork the test tube with a cork and insert a glass tube into the test tube through the hole in the cork.
Blow exhaled air into the test tube through the glass tube.
When exhaled air is blown, the CO2(g) it contains turns the lime water milky.
In this reaction, quick lime and water combine to form a single product: slaked lime (calcium hydroxide). So this is a combination reaction.
